conventions.convention: The gauge groups used here are smooth adjoint-group sections with the finite-atlas C∞ section topology. The based subgroup consists of sections evaluating to the identity in the chosen frame; the reduced group is the quotient by constant central sections Z_N. The conclusions do not silently substitute Sobolev groups.
For C_f = S² ∪_f D⁴, the Hopf invariant is the integer H(f) determined by x² = H(f)y, where x restricts to the positive bottom-sphere generator and y is determined by the oriented attached cell.
Reduced suspension collapses both end slices and the basepoint track. Its pinch sends the first half of the suspension coordinate to the first wedge summand and the second half to the second summand.
Complex orientations give H(h) = +1; the product orientation on S² × S² gives Hopf invariant +2 for its folded top-cell attachment.

Relative section smoothing requires the prescribed family on the closed collared parameter submanifold to be continuous in the full C∞ section topology. Marked spatial fiber values are fixed throughout approximation and homotopy.

Hemisphere representatives satisfy f_+(q) = ψ(q)f_-(q)ψ(q)⁻¹, and the based point is the upper-disk center. Component identifications are pointed-set bijections; positive homotopy-degree identifications are group isomorphisms.

Weak contractibility means path connectedness together with vanishing of every positive based homotopy group. The section obstruction assumes a nonempty locally trivial right principal topological bundle.

load_bearing.statement: For every smooth principal SU(N) bundle P over S^r, r ∈ {3,4}, N ≥ 2, the smooth based gauge group satisfies π_j(G_m(P),e) ≅ π_{j+r}(SU(N),e) for j ≥ 1 and has a pointed component-set bijection π_0(G_m(P),e) ≅ π_r(SU(N),e), independently of the clutching class.
For every smooth principal SU(N) bundle over S^r, r ∈ {3,4}, N ≥ 2, the reduced smooth gauge group has infinitely many path components when r = 3 and nontrivial fundamental group when r = 4.

For the stated compact connected oriented boundaryless smooth Riemannian base of dimension 3 or 4 and smooth principal SU(N) bundle, inclusion of smooth gauge sections into continuous gauge sections induces component bijections and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups, both for the full groups and for the subgroups fixed at the chosen frame.

For every stated sphere bundle, evaluation of smooth gauge sections at the chosen frame is a numerable locally trivial bundle with based gauge-group fiber, and quotient by Z_N is a finite covering. Both maps are Serre fibrations.
For every N ≥ 2, SU(N) is path connected, π_1(SU(N)) = π_2(SU(N)) = 0, and π_3(SU(N)) ≅ Z. Also π_4(SU(2)) ≅ Z/2 and π_5(SU(2)) ≠ 0.
For every integer N ≥ 2, π_5(SU(N)) is nonzero.
Set η_2 = h and η_j = Σ^{j−2}h for j ≥ 2. For every n ≥ 2, η_n ∘ η_{n+1}: S^{n+2} → S^n is not nullhomotopic.

Under the stated compact-manifold, collared-relative-family and fixed-fiber-value hypotheses, every continuous family of finite-rank vector-bundle sections admits arbitrarily close approximation by a C∞-continuous family of smooth sections, preserving the relative family and marked values, with a straight-line homotopy preserving those constraints.

A continuous section of a nonempty locally trivial principal topological H-bundle makes H a retract of its total space. If the total space is weakly contractible, H is path connected and all π_j(H,e), j ≥ 1, vanish.

seams_checked.note: Opened the configuration definition. Consumers preserve its smooth C∞ section topology, frame evaluation, adjoint transition and finite-center quotient conventions. The continuous-section model is introduced separately and related by the locally proved smoothing lemma.

The example uses the defined smooth groups and quotient topology for the trivial SU(2) bundle over S³, with a chosen frame. It does not infer a Sobolev conclusion or extend its example-specific claim to S⁴.

Opened the Singer-obstruction consumer. Its F5 preserves the all-sector S³ component and S⁴ fundamental-group conclusions; F6 preserves the nonempty locally trivial principal-bundle and weak-contractibility hypotheses. Their use in proof step 3.1 is faithful. The evaluation and retraction diagrams in the assigned items have consistent arrows and compositions.
